candidate.title: TruSeq Small RNA
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq Small RNA product/library-preparation schematic: a small RNA fragment is adaptor-ligated, primed, reverse transcribed, then denatured and amplified to a P5/P7-bearing indexed DNA library ready for cluster generation. No kit revision or alternative method is identified. The four captioned transformations are the extraction units; the lower primer/template intermediate belongs to the combined Denature and amplify operation. This is a schematic architecture rather than a complete protocol or a primary-paper implementation.

The schematic starts with a fragment; production or isolation of that fragment is outside this depiction.

Cluster generation is a downstream interface named by the final caption; clusters and sequence data are not depicted.

operations.label: Ligate adaptors
operations.description: Attach the two different terminal adaptor segments to the small RNA fragment, producing one adaptor-flanked RNA molecule. This caption groups adaptor ligation; it does not specify separate 3′-first or 5′-first reactions.
operations.mechanism: Ligation, as explicitly named; the drawing does not specify enzymes or reactive terminal groups.
operations.information_effect: The RNA insert remains between distinguishable terminal adaptor regions, providing the physical substrate for subsequent adaptor-directed priming.

evidence.locator: First downward arrow, 'Ligate adaptors', and product labeled '5′ Adaptor' and '3′ Adaptor'

operations.label: Add primer
operations.description: Add the short primer shown aligned beneath the 3′ adaptor of the adaptor-ligated RNA. The output differs by the associated primer, before an extended copy is drawn.
operations.mechanism: Primer association with the 3′ adaptor is inferred from the aligned short green segment.
operations.information_effect: The bound primer connects the ligated 3′ adaptor to the following reverse-transcription step.

evidence.locator: Second downward arrow, 'Add primer', and short green strand below the right-hand adaptor
'Add primer' product followed by 'Reverse transcription'
evidence.rationale: The short strand at the 3′ adaptor is the primer for the next named copying operation.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Extend the bound primer to form the depicted longer complementary strand across the adaptor-flanked RNA template, yielding an RNA/cDNA intermediate.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated DNA synthesis is the meaning of the named reverse-transcription step; no particular enzyme or reaction setting is supplied.
operations.information_effect: The insert sequence is represented in a complementary DNA strand, so the downstream library can carry information about the original small RNA through a DNA copy.

evidence.locator: Third downward arrow, 'Reverse transcription', and two aligned strands below it
'Reverse transcription' and replacement of the short lower strand by an extended strand
evidence.rationale: The caption identifies RNA-to-DNA copying; the new strand spans the same insert/adaptor positions, supporting transfer of sequence information into cDNA.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Process the reverse-transcribed material through the depicted separated-template/primer intermediate and amplify it into the full-length two-strand library. The intermediate shows P5-bearing and Index 1/P7-bearing primer extensions, which appear as terminal/index segments of the final product. The two lower arrows and this intermediate are retained within the single combined source-caption block; the drawing does not resolve a complete internal synthesis sequence.
operations.mechanism: Denaturation and amplification are explicitly named. Primer-mediated incorporation of the terminal/index segments is inferred from their positions on the intermediate and the resulting full-length product.
operations.information_effect: Amplified DNA carries an insert derived from the small RNA together with the displayed Index region and P5/P7 cluster-generation interface. A downstream insert sequence can therefore represent the original fragment by the copying route. The schematic establishes neither capture efficiency nor a calibration between final library copy number and starting RNA abundance. No index-to-sample assignment is shown.
